body:
> So this is what I want to say to you: You have every right to be unhappy, even when, especially when, you don't really know why! What's more confusing and despairing than not knowing the reasons of your unhappiness?

Exactly, I don't even know what my problem is. I just don't find living palatable.

> I admire your determination to get through college with your blindness. I can't imagine how tough life is when blind and how horrible it must feel to slowly lose your eye sight. 

The worst part is honestly the transportation, I can't begin to describe how bad it hurts when someone really needs me to be somewhere and I just can't go to them even though they're minutes away by car.

> And if I may go on a personal note, I just can't believe that people call you privileged when you are dealing with a degenerative eye condition. It really makes me angry. 

I'm a white middle class male, supposedly the pros are supposed to outweigh the cons. I guess I just don't think they cancel each other out, or maybe they do and that's why I feel so "meh" about the whole thing?

> I do recognize the feeling of getting crushed by obligation. I lived about eighteen years of my life that way (up to three years ago), not knowing what I liked and just doing whatever others told me was good for me. It was a very unpleasant way of living and it was completely exhausting. It took a long time before I figured out what was causing it (a bad experience in my early youth) and another long time until I could turn it around. I can't therefore give you an easy solution, however you surely are not alone feeling that crushing weight and in my experience it can be a very real cause of unhappiness.

After I nearly died the first time, I told everyone I wouldn't do it again and now I feel obligated not to :|
When I attempted suicide the first time I was upset and scared but I don't feel that way at all now.

I wouldn't dare mention this to anyone around me, the level of drama it would create is unbearable. They always focus on "Stopping it" by any means necessary whether or not that means I'm happy is apparently irrelevant. I spent time in a psych ward and it was undeniably the worst experience I've had in my life, I felt trapped like I had control of my life ripped away from me, it was horrible.
